quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
rationale: The Agreement contains a vendor-side defence and indemnity that meets the preferred position on its material terms. Kubient defends, indemnifies and holds harmless AP and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees against all third-party Claims (expressly including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or in connection with the Services (p0048), the Auction Platform (p0049), Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors (p0051). Third-party IP infringement is captured: claims "arising out of or in connection with" the Services and the Auction Platform reach infringement allegations, and limb (iv) indemnifies breach of Kubient's warranties, which include that it owns or controls the rights granted to AP and is the rightful owner or licensee of all IP rights to the Service, Auction Platform and products delivered (p0039, p0040). Kubient's compliance-with-Law warranty (p0041) and the acts/omissions limb likewise pick up breach of law, Vendor-caused data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Standard procedure is present (prompt notice, indemnitor control of defence with no liability-admitting settlement without consent, cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost), and notice delay does not relieve the indemnifying party — a pro-AP formulation. The indemnity is uncapped in practice: p0027 carves "THE PARTIES' LIABILITY FOR INDEMNIFICATION" out of the consequential-damages exclusion, and no super-cap or sub-cap is imposed, so the fallback's 3x-fees ceiling is not needed. AP's own indemnity (p0052) is directionally correct — keyed to its Content and Properties, unauthorised or inappropriate use, and its own breach and acts/omissions — with no reciprocal indemnity for Kubient's Services. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: the Creative limb (p0050) carries a "to the best of its knowledge" qualifier, and AP's indemnity extends slightly beyond Customer-provided content and breach of law to unauthorised use and breach of any representation or warranty. Neither is material, and per playbook semantics these are recorded here instead of being redlined. No walk-away condition exists.

The fallback requires a mutual cap of 12 months' fees with carve-outs, so the absence of any cap fails the fallback on a material term and leaves our own direct liability unlimited. Because this is a revenue-share arrangement in which Customer pays no fees to Kubient (Section 5: payment flows from Kubient to Customer), a pure "fees paid by Customer" basis would be illusory; the redline therefore adopts the preferred greater-of formulation using amounts paid or payable between the Parties and a USD 1,000,000 floor, adds the standard uncapped carve-outs, and confirms revenue-share amounts owed are not "damages" for cap purposes. As between the Parties, Customer is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title and interest in and to the Content, the Properties, the Inventory, the Requests and all data and visitor information collected from or through the Content, the Properties or the Inventory (collectively, "Customer Data"), together with all intellectual property rights therein. quote: The initial term of this Agreement shall be one (1) year from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term"). This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
rationale: Section 4(a) sits at the playbook fallback, so we are not redlining it. The committed period is a 1-year Initial Term (not a multi-year commitment), and the detection standard only treats the absence of a convenience right as a deviation where the term exceeds 12 months. Following the Initial Term, AP holds a symmetric convenience right on ninety (90) days' written notice, which is inside the fallback's 60–90 day window. Kubient's own convenience right is not confined to term-end, but it requires 90 days' notice and so does not reach the walk-away threshold of "fewer than 90 days' notice"; the Initial Term lock-out prevents Kubient from exiting mid-term. On the money side, Kubient's entitlement to "all fees generated during the termination period" is effectively limited to the 90-day notice period (approximately three months' fees), consistent with the fallback cap of no more than 3 months' fees, and it applies equally whichever party terminates. Noted but not flagged: we do not get the preferred 30-day notice, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — that mechanic is inapplicable here because Section 5 is a revenue-share under which Kubient pays AP rather than AP prepaying fees. Kubient's convenience right not being restricted to the end of a renewal term is likewise a sub-element short of the preferred wording rather than a material failure.

quote: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. rationale: Renewal term length is acceptable (successive 1-year, not multi-year), but the only exit route after the Initial Term is a ninety (90) day notice, which exceeds the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal window and so fails the fallback on a material term (it is at, not beyond, the 90-day walk-away line). proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and data-return obligation in Section 4(c)

quote: (iv) and each Party will return or destroy any of the other Party's Confidential Information then in its possession.
rationale: Section 4(c) is the only effect-of-termination provision: Kubient ceases the Services, the licence is revoked, Customer stops using the Auction Platform, and each Party may "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at its own election. There is no transition-assistance obligation and no right for AP to receive its Content, Requests or other data back in a usable format, and no deletion certification; searches for transition/migration/export/data-return language return nothing elsewhere in the Agreement. Because Kubient could elect destruction, this sits at or near the walk-away position (no data return / immediate deletion), failing even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days). We therefore insert a new paragraph 4(c)(v) reflecting the preferred position — up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification — expressly overriding the destroy option for Customer Data, and flag the 90-day fallback in the comment.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: The rule expects a transition-assistance and data-return clause; the only effect-of-termination provision (4(c)(i)-(iv)) covers cessation of services, licence revocation and a mutual 'return or destroy' election for Confidential Information, with no transition assistance, no data export in a usable format and no deletion certification — 'missing' is the correct classification and not double-flagged elsewhere. The inserted 4(c)(v) tracks the playbook model language closely (six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, deletion plus written certification) and is a targeted addition appended after 4(c)(iv) rather than a rewrite of existing text. The precedence sentence over 4(c)(iv) is a necessary and minimal addition, since the existing destroy-at-election right would otherwise defeat the data-return obligation identified in the rationale. Comment is accurate, concise, in the required first-person plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, explains the change, and offers the 90-day fallback; deterministic checks corroborate that transition/data-return language is present in the redline.

quote: (vi) any services provided by it shall comply with the terms of this Agreement and shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility;

ops.text: Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, to the extent Kubient collects, stores, processes or otherwise has access to Customer data or visitor information, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000.
